nodes.name: IsPicardLindelof.exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
nodes.lean:
existence of a local solution whose initial point `x` may be different from the centre `x₀` of
the closed ball within which the properties of the vector field hold. -/
theorem exists_eq_forall_mem_Icc_hasDerivWithinAt
    (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) :
    ∃ α : ℝ → E, α t₀ = x ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, HasDerivWithinAt α (f t (α t)) (Icc tmin tmax) t := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := FunSpace.exists_isFixedPt_next hf hx
  refine ⟨α.compProj, by rw [FunSpace.compProj_val, ← hα, FunSpace.next_apply₀], fun t ht ↦ ?_⟩
  apply hasDerivWithinAt_picard_Icc t₀.property hf.continuousOn_uncurry
    α.continuous_compProj.continuousOn (fun _ ht' ↦ α.compProj_mem_closedBall hf.mul_max_le)
    x ht |>.congr_of_mem _ ht
  intro t' ht'

theorem ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc
    (hv : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, LipschitzOnWith K (v t) (s t))
    (ht : t₀ ∈ Ioo a b)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hf' : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (v t (f t)) t)
    (hfs : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, f t ∈ s t)
    (hg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b))
    (hg' : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt g (v t (g t)) t)
    (hgs : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, g t ∈ s t)
    (heq : f t₀ = g t₀) :
    EqOn f g (Icc a b) := by
  rw [← Icc_union_Icc_eq_Icc (le_of_lt ht.1) (le_of_lt ht.2)]
  apply EqOn.union
  · have hss : Ioc a t₀ ⊆ Ioo a b := Ioc_subset_Ioo_right ht.2
    exact ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_left (fun t ht ↦ hv t (hss ht))
      (hf.mono <| Icc_subset_Icc_right <| le_of_lt ht.2)
      (fun _ ht' ↦ (hf' _ (hss ht')).hasDerivWithinAt) (fun _ ht' ↦ (hfs _ (hss ht')))
      (hg.mono <| Icc_subset_Icc_right <| le_of_lt ht.2)
      (fun _ ht' ↦ (hg' _ (hss ht')).hasDerivWithinAt) (fun _ ht' ↦ (hgs _ (hss ht'))) heq
  · have hss : Ico t₀ b ⊆ Ioo a b := Ico_subset_Ioo_left ht.1
    exact ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_right (fun t ht ↦ hv t (hss ht))
      (hf.mono <| Icc_subset_Icc_left <| le_of_lt ht.1)
      (fun _ ht' ↦ (hf' _ (hss ht')).hasDerivWithinAt) (fun _ ht' ↦ (hfs _ (hss ht')))
      (hg.mono <| Icc_subset_Icc_left <| le_of_lt ht.1)
      (fun _ ht' ↦ (hg' _ (hss ht')).hasDerivWithinAt) (fun _ ht' ↦ (hgs _ (hss ht'))) heq

nodes.name: IsPicardLindelof
nodes.lean:
`IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K`, where `t₀ ∈ Icc tmin tmax`, means that the time-dependent vector
field `f` satisfies the conditions to admit an integral curve `α : ℝ → E` to `f` defined on
`Icc tmin tmax` with the initial condition `α t₀ = x`, where `‖x - x₀‖ ≤ r`. Note that the initial
point `x` is allowed to differ from the point `x₀` about which the conditions on `f` are stated. -/
structure IsPicardLindelof {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    (f : ℝ → E → E) {tmin tmax : ℝ} (t₀ : Icc tmin tmax) (x₀ : E) (a r L K : ℝ≥0) : Prop where
  /-- The vector field at any time is Lipschitz with constant `K` within a closed ball. -/
  lipschitzOnWith : ∀ t ∈ Icc tmin tmax, LipschitzOnWith K (f t) (closedBall x₀ a)
  /-- The vector field is continuous in time within a closed ball. -/
  continuousOn : ∀ x ∈ closedBall x₀ a, ContinuousOn (f · x) (Icc tmin tmax)
  /-- `L` is an upper bound of the norm of the vector field. -/

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace
nodes.lean:
structure FunSpace {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    {tmin tmax : ℝ} (t₀ : Icc tmin tmax) (x₀ : E) (r L : ℝ≥0) where
  /-- The domain is `Icc tmin tmax`. -/
  toFun : Icc tmin tmax → E
  lipschitzWith : LipschitzWith L toFun
  mem_closedBall₀ : toFun t₀ ∈ closedBall x₀ r

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.instCompleteSpace
nodes.lean:
/-- We show that `FunSpace` is complete in order to apply the contraction mapping theorem. -/
instance [CompleteSpace E] : CompleteSpace (FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L) := by
  rw [completeSpace_iff_isComplete_range isUniformInducing_toContinuousMap]
  apply IsClosed.isComplete
  rw [range_toContinuousMap, ofPred_and]
  apply isClosed_setOfPred_lipschitzWith L |>.preimage continuous_coeFun |>.inter
  simp_rw [mem_closedBall_iff_norm]
  exact isClosed_le (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)

nodes.name: ODE.picard
nodes.lean:
/-- The Picard iteration. It will be shown that if `α : ℝ → E` and `picard f t₀ x₀ α` agree on an
interval containing `t₀`, then `α` is a solution to `f` with `α t₀ = x₀` on this interval. -/
noncomputable def picard (f : ℝ → E → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (x₀ : E) (α : ℝ → E) : ℝ → E :=
  fun t ↦ x₀ + ∫ τ in t₀..t, f τ (α τ)

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.next
nodes.lean:
/-- The map on `FunSpace` defined by `picard`, some `n`-th iterate of which will be a contracting
map -/
noncomputable def next (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r)
    (α : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L) : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L where
  toFun t := picard f t₀ x α.compProj t
  lipschitzWith := LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul fun t₁ t₂ ↦ by
    rw [dist_eq_norm, picard_apply, picard_apply, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub,
      integral_interval_sub_left (intervalIntegrable_comp_compProj hf _ t₁)
        (intervalIntegrable_comp_compProj hf _ t₂), Subtype.dist_eq, Real.dist_eq]
    apply intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const
    intro t ht
    -- Can `grind` do this in the future?
    have ht : t ∈ Icc tmin tmax :=
      subset_trans uIoc_subset_uIcc (uIcc_subset_Icc t₂.property t₁.property) ht
    exact hf.norm_le _ ht _ <| α.mem_closedBall hf.mul_max_le
  mem_closedBall₀ := by simp [hx]

/-- A time-dependent bound on the distance between the `n`-th iterates of `next` on two curves -/
lemma dist_iterate_next_apply_le (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K)
    (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) (α β : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L) (n : ℕ) (t : Icc tmin tmax) :
    dist ((next hf hx)^[n] α t) ((next hf hx)^[n] β t) ≤
      (K * |t.val - t₀.val|) ^ n / n ! * dist α β := by
  induction n generalizing t with
  | zero => simpa using!
      ContinuousMap.dist_apply_le_dist (f := toContinuousMap α) (g := toContinuousMap β) _
  | succ n hn =>
    rw [iterate_succ_apply', iterate_succ_apply', dist_eq_norm, next_apply,
      next_apply, picard_apply, picard_apply, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub,
      ← intervalIntegral.integral_sub (intervalIntegrable_comp_compProj hf _ t)
        (intervalIntegrable_comp_compProj hf _ t)]
    calc
      _ ≤ ∫ τ in uIoc t₀.val t.val, K ^ (n + 1) * |τ - t₀| ^ n / n ! * dist α β := by
        rw [intervalIntegral.norm_intervalIntegral_eq]
        apply MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le (Continuous.integrableOn_uIoc (by fun_prop))
        apply ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioc |>.mono
        intro t' ht'
        -- Can `grind` do this in the future?
        have ht' : t' ∈ Icc tmin tmax :=
          subset_trans uIoc_subset_uIcc (uIcc_subset_Icc t₀.property t.property) ht'
        rw [← dist_eq_norm, compProj_of_mem, compProj_of_mem]
        exact dist_comp_iterate_next_le hf hx _ ⟨t', ht'⟩ (hn _)
      _ ≤ (K * |t.val - t₀.val|) ^ (n + 1) / (n + 1) ! * dist α β := by
        apply le_of_abs_le
        -- critical: `integral_pow_abs_sub_uIoc`
        rw [← intervalIntegral.abs_intervalIntegral_eq, intervalIntegral.integral_mul_const,
          intervalIntegral.integral_div, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, abs_mul, abs_div,
          abs_mul, intervalIntegral.abs_intervalIntegral_eq, integral_pow_abs_sub_uIoc, abs_div,
          abs_pow, abs_pow, abs_dist, NNReal.abs_eq, abs_abs, mul_div, div_div, ← abs_mul,
          ← Nat.cast_succ, ← Nat.cast_mul, ← Nat.factorial_succ, Nat.abs_cast, ← mul_pow]

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.dist_iterate_next_iterate_next_le
nodes.lean:
/-- The `n`-th iterate of `next` is Lipschitz continuous with respect to `FunSpace`, with constant
$(K \max(t_{\mathrm{max}}, t_{\mathrm{min}})^n / n!$. -/
lemma dist_iterate_next_iterate_next_le (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K)
    (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) (α β : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L) (n : ℕ) :
    dist ((next hf hx)^[n] α) ((next hf hx)^[n] β) ≤
      (K * max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin)) ^ n / n ! * dist α β := by
  rw [← MetricSpace.isometry_induced FunSpace.toContinuousMap FunSpace.toContinuousMap.injective
    |>.dist_eq, ContinuousMap.dist_le]
  · intro t
    apply le_trans <| dist_iterate_next_apply_le hf hx α β n t
    gcongr
    exact abs_sub_le_max_sub t.property.1 t.property.2 _
  · have : 0 ≤ max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin) := le_max_of_le_left <| sub_nonneg_of_le t₀.property.2
    positivity

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.exists_contractingWith_iterate_next
nodes.lean:
/-- Some `n`-th iterate of `next` is a contracting map, and its associated Lipschitz constant is
independent of the initial point. -/
lemma exists_contractingWith_iterate_next (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (C : ℝ≥0), ∀ (x : E) (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r),
      ContractingWith C (next hf hx)^[n] := by
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := FloorSemiring.tendsto_pow_div_factorial_atTop (K * max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin))
    |>.eventually (gt_mem_nhds zero_lt_one) |>.exists
  have : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (K * max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin)) ^ n / n ! := by
    have : 0 ≤ max (tmax - t₀) (t₀ - tmin) := le_max_of_le_left <| sub_nonneg_of_le t₀.property.2
    positivity
  refine ⟨n, ⟨_, this⟩, fun x hx ↦ ?_⟩
  exact ⟨hn, LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul fun α β ↦ dist_iterate_next_iterate_next_le hf hx α β n⟩

nodes.name: ContractingWith.isFixedPt_fixedPoint_iterate
nodes.lean:
theorem isFixedPt_fixedPoint_iterate {n : ℕ} (hf : ContractingWith K f^[n]) :
    IsFixedPt f (hf.fixedPoint f^[n]) := by
  set x := hf.fixedPoint f^[n]
  have hx : f^[n] x = x := hf.fixedPoint_isFixedPt
  have := hf.toLipschitzWith.dist_le_mul x (f x)
  rw [← iterate_succ_apply, iterate_succ_apply', hx] at this
  contrapose! this

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.exists_isFixedPt_next
nodes.lean:
/-- The map `next` has a fixed point in the space of curves. This will be used to construct a
solution `α : ℝ → E` to the ODE. -/
lemma exists_isFixedPt_next [CompleteSpace E] (hf : IsPicardLindelof f t₀ x₀ a r L K)
    (hx : x ∈ closedBall x₀ r) :
    ∃ α : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L, IsFixedPt (next hf hx) α :=
  let ⟨_, _, h⟩ := exists_contractingWith_iterate_next hf
  ⟨_, h x hx |>.isFixedPt_fixedPoint_iterate⟩

nodes.name: ODE.FunSpace.compProj
nodes.lean:
/-- Extend the domain of `α` from `Icc tmin tmax` to `ℝ` such that `α t = α tmin` for all `t ≤ tmin`
and `α t = α tmax` for all `t ≥ tmax`. -/
noncomputable def compProj (α : FunSpace t₀ x₀ r L) (t : ℝ) : E :=
  α <| projIcc tmin tmax (le_trans t₀.property.1 t₀.property.2) t

/-- A time-reversed version of `ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_right`. Uniqueness is shown in a
closed interval `Icc a b`, where `b` is the "initial" time. -/
theorem ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_left
    (hv : ∀ t ∈ Ioc a b, LipschitzOnWith K (v t) (s t))
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hf' : ∀ t ∈ Ioc a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (v t (f t)) (Iic t) t)
    (hfs : ∀ t ∈ Ioc a b, f t ∈ s t)
    (hg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b))
    (hg' : ∀ t ∈ Ioc a b, HasDerivWithinAt g (v t (g t)) (Iic t) t)
    (hgs : ∀ t ∈ Ioc a b, g t ∈ s t)
    (hb : f b = g b) :
    EqOn f g (Icc a b) := by
  have hv' : ∀ t ∈ Ico (-b) (-a), LipschitzOnWith K (Neg.neg ∘ (v (-t))) (s (-t)) := by
    intro t ht
    replace ht : -t ∈ Ioc a b := by
      push _ ∈ _ at ht ⊢
      constructor <;> linarith
    rw [← one_mul K]
    exact LipschitzWith.id.neg.comp_lipschitzOnWith (hv _ ht)
  have hmt1 : MapsTo Neg.neg (Icc (-b) (-a)) (Icc a b) :=
    fun _ ht ↦ ⟨le_neg.mp ht.2, neg_le.mp ht.1⟩
  have hmt2 : MapsTo Neg.neg (Ico (-b) (-a)) (Ioc a b) :=
    fun _ ht ↦ ⟨lt_neg.mp ht.2, neg_le.mp ht.1⟩
  have hmt3 (t : ℝ) : MapsTo Neg.neg (Ici t) (Iic (-t)) :=
    fun _ ht' ↦ mem_Iic.mpr <| neg_le_neg ht'
  suffices EqOn (f ∘ Neg.neg) (g ∘ Neg.neg) (Icc (-b) (-a)) by
    rw [eqOn_comp_right_iff] at this
    convert this
    simp
  apply ODE_solution_unique_of_mem_Icc_right hv'
    (hf.comp continuousOn_neg hmt1) _ (fun _ ht ↦ hfs _ (hmt2 ht))
    (hg.comp continuousOn_neg hmt1) _ (fun _ ht ↦ hgs _ (hmt2 ht)) (by simp [hb])
  · intro t ht
    convert
      HasFDerivWithinAt.comp_hasDerivWithinAt t (hf' (-t) (hmt2 ht))
        (hasDerivAt_neg t).hasDerivWithinAt (hmt3 t)
    simp
  · intro t ht
    convert
      HasFDerivWithinAt.comp_hasDerivWithinAt t (hg' (-t) (hmt2 ht))
        (hasDerivAt_neg t).hasDerivWithinAt (hmt3 t)
    simp

theorem dist_le_of_trajectories_ODE_of_mem
    (hv : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, LipschitzOnWith K (v t) (s t))
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hf' : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (v t (f t)) (Ici t) t)

nodes.name: norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le
nodes.lean:
/-- A Grönwall-like inequality: if `f : ℝ → E` is continuous on `[a, b]`, has right derivative
`f' x` at every point `x ∈ [a, b)`, and satisfies the inequalities `‖f a‖ ≤ δ`,
`∀ x ∈ [a, b), ‖f' x‖ ≤ K * ‖f x‖ + ε`, then `‖f x‖` is bounded by `gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)`
on `[a, b]`. -/
theorem norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le {f f' : ℝ → E} {δ K ε : ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ici x) x)
    (ha : ‖f a‖ ≤ δ) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ‖f' x‖ ≤ K * ‖f x‖ + ε) :
    ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ‖f x‖ ≤ gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a) :=
  le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le (continuous_norm.comp_continuousOn hf)
    (fun x hx _r hr => (hf' x hx).liminf_right_slope_norm_le hr) ha bound

/-- Let `f : [a, b] → E` be a differentiable function such that `f a = 0`
and `‖f'(x)‖ ≤ K ‖f(x)‖` for some constant `K`. Then `f = 0` on `[a, b]`. -/
theorem eq_zero_of_abs_deriv_le_mul_abs_self_of_eq_zero_right {f f' : ℝ → E} {K a b : ℝ}
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Ici x) x)
    (ha : f a = 0) (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ‖f' x‖ ≤ K * ‖f x‖) :
    ∀ x ∈ Set.Icc a b, f x = 0 := by
  intro x hx
  apply norm_le_zero_iff.mp
  calc ‖f x‖
    _ ≤ gronwallBound 0 K 0 (x - a) :=
      norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le hf hf' (by simp [ha]) (by simpa using bound) _ hx
    _ = 0 := by rw [gronwallBound_ε0_δ0]

variable {v : ℝ → E → E} {s : ℝ → Set E} {K : ℝ≥0} {f g f' g' : ℝ → E} {a b : ℝ} {εf εg δ : ℝ}

/-- If `f` and `g` are two approximate solutions of the same ODE, then the distance between them
can't grow faster than exponentially. This is a simple corollary of Grönwall's inequality, and some
people call this Grönwall's inequality too.

nodes.statement: E is a complete real normed space; the closed time interval I contains t₀.

On the closed ball around x₀ of radius a, the field is uniformly K-Lipschitz in state, continuous in time, and bounded by L. The interval size satisfies L·R ≤ a−r, where R is the greater distance from t₀ to an endpoint. The initial point x lies in the radius-r ball.
Use interval-valued Lipschitz curves with the initial-ball constraint and the supremum metric. Completeness follows by identifying a closed subset of continuous maps.
The admissible curve space X is a nonempty complete metric space.
Integrate the field along a candidate curve. The field bound and the interval-size hypothesis keep the construction admissible.
The Picard integral formula Tα(t)=x+∫ₜ₀ᵗ f(s,α(s)) ds defines a self-map T of the admissible curve space.
Induct on n, bound differences of vector-field values using Lipschitz continuity, integrate the power of elapsed time, then take the supremum over the interval.
The distance between Tⁿα and Tⁿβ is bounded by ((K·R)ⁿ/n!) times the distance between α and β.
Use convergence of (K·R)ⁿ/n! to zero to choose n with a Lipschitz coefficient less than one.
There is an iterate Tⁿ that is a contraction on the admissible curve space.

fact:state-space.title: Complete state space and time interval
fact:state-space.summary: The existence argument takes place in a real Banach space and starts at a time belonging to the closed interval.
fact:state-space.why_here: Completeness supports the curve-space construction and the state-space integration used to obtain the solution.

fact:existence-hypotheses.title: Field bounds and starting region
fact:existence-hypotheses.summary: On the radius-a ball the field is uniformly K-Lipschitz in state, continuous in time, and bounded in norm by L. The initial state lies within radius r, and the maximum travel budget LR is at most a−r, where R is the largest time distance from the initial time to an endpoint.
fact:existence-hypotheses.why_here: These controls keep the update admissible, bound differences of iterates, and support differentiation of the integral.

step:curve-space.title: Completeness in the supremum metric
step:curve-space.summary: Start with continuous curves into the complete state space, with distance given by the supremum of their pointwise distances. Uniform limits preserve the Lipschitz bound and the closed initial-ball constraint, so the admissible subset is closed and complete. The constant curve at the ball center is admissible, giving nonemptiness.
step:curve-space.why_here: This constructs the complete metric space needed for the fixed-point argument.

fact:curve-space.title: Complete admissible curve space
fact:curve-space.summary: The space X of admissible curves is nonempty and complete in the supremum metric.
fact:curve-space.why_here: It is the domain of the Picard self-map and the complete space on which the contracting iterate has a fixed point.

step:picard-self-map.title: Picard operator preserves admissibility
step:picard-self-map.summary: An admissible curve stays within distance r+LR of the ball center, so the field bound applies along the curve. The difference between two output values is an integral between the two times, with norm at most L times their distance. The output starts at the prescribed state, so it satisfies both defining constraints.
step:picard-self-map.why_here: The field and time bounds make the integral operation repeatable on the same curve space.

fact:picard-self-map.title: Picard update on admissible curves
fact:picard-self-map.summary: For the prescribed initial state x, the map T sends an admissible curve to the curve obtained by integrating the field along it and adding x.
fact:picard-self-map.why_here: It gives both the operator to iterate and the formula to substitute into the fixed-point identity.

step:factorial-bound.title: Factorial estimate by induction
step:factorial-bound.summary: At iteration zero, the pointwise distance is bounded by the supremum distance. At each successor step, spatial Lipschitz continuity contributes a factor K, and integrating the elapsed-time power changes the factor |t−t₀|ⁿ/n! to |t−t₀|ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)!. Replacing elapsed time by R and taking the supremum gives the operator bound.
step:factorial-bound.why_here: This produces a uniform coefficient for the iterated map from pointwise integral estimates.

fact:factorial-bound.title: Lipschitz bound for Picard iterates
fact:factorial-bound.summary: In the supremum metric, the distance between the nth iterates is bounded by the starting distance times the factorial coefficient.
fact:factorial-bound.why_here: This coefficient can be made smaller than one to obtain a contraction.

step:contracting-iterate.title: Choose a contracting iterate
step:contracting-iterate.summary: The Lipschitz coefficients are bounded by (KR)ⁿ/n!, which tends to zero for fixed K and R. Choose an iteration count for which the coefficient is strictly below one. The uniform distance estimate then makes that iterate a contraction.
step:contracting-iterate.why_here: The choice supplies the contraction needed for the fixed-point step.

fact:contracting-iterate.title: A power of the Picard map contracts
fact:contracting-iterate.summary: There is an iteration count for which the iterated Picard map has a Lipschitz constant strictly below one on the admissible space.
fact:contracting-iterate.why_here: It supplies the contraction premise for obtaining a curve fixed by the original update.

step:fixed-curve.title: Banach’s fixed-point theorem
step:fixed-curve.summary: The contracting iterate acts on the nonempty complete curve space, so Banach’s theorem gives its unique fixed point. Applying the original Picard map to that point gives another fixed point of the iterate because the maps commute. Uniqueness shows that the original map fixes the same curve.
step:fixed-curve.why_here: It turns the contraction estimate into an admissible curve satisfying the Picard identity.

fact:fixed-curve.title: An admissible fixed curve exists
fact:fixed-curve.summary: For the prescribed starting state, there is an admissible curve fixed by the Picard update. The next step uses such a curve as its witness.
fact:fixed-curve.why_here: A fixed curve supplies the local witness whose extension satisfies the integral equation.

step:integral-equation.title: Unfold the Picard fixed-point identity
step:integral-equation.summary: Take the admissible fixed curve and extend it by its endpoint values. On the original interval the extension agrees with the curve, and the fixed-point identity says that its values equal the Picard update. Substituting the update formula gives the integral equation there.
step:integral-equation.why_here: It expresses the fixed-point condition in the integral form needed for differentiation.

fact:integral-equation.title: Integral equation for the extended curve
fact:integral-equation.summary: The chosen extended curve agrees on the time interval with its prescribed initial state plus the integral of the field along that same curve.
fact:integral-equation.statement_latex: \forall t\in I,\quad g(t)=x+\int_{t_0}^{t} f(s,g(s))\,ds,\qquad g\text{ is the endpoint extension of the chosen Picard fixed curve}.
fact:integral-equation.why_here: This equality gives both the initial value and a formula to differentiate.

step:ode-solution.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus
step:ode-solution.summary: At the initial time the integral has identical limits, so the extended curve takes the prescribed value x. The field is jointly continuous on the region traversed by the curve, using time continuity and the uniform state Lipschitz bound. The fundamental theorem gives the derivative of the integral expression within the interval, and equality on the interval transfers that derivative to the extended curve.
step:ode-solution.why_here: This verifies the initial value and the ODE for the chosen witness.

fact:ode-solution.title: Existence of an interval solution
fact:ode-solution.summary: The extended curve witnesses the existence of a real-line function taking the prescribed value at the initial time and satisfying the ODE by derivatives within the closed interval.
fact:ode-solution.why_here: This is the explicit existential conclusion of the existence argument.

fact:uniqueness-hypotheses.title: Interior trajectory hypotheses
fact:uniqueness-hypotheses.summary: The two trajectories are continuous on the closed interval. At each interior time both solve the ODE and lie in the permitted state set, where the field has a uniform state Lipschitz constant. The comparison time is strictly interior.
fact:uniqueness-hypotheses.why_here: These hypotheses can be restricted to the two half-intervals with the required one-sided derivatives.

fact:same-initial-value.title: Common value at the initial time
fact:same-initial-value.summary: The two given trajectories meet at the specified interior time.
fact:same-initial-value.why_here: This supplies the common endpoint value for both applications of one-sided uniqueness.

step:trajectory-comparison.title: Grönwall’s inequality
step:trajectory-comparison.summary: For two forward trajectories in the permitted sets, the derivative of their difference is the difference of the two field values. Its norm is bounded by K times the norm of the trajectory difference. Grönwall’s inequality gives a reusable exponential bound from an initial separation at most δ. In the supplied exact-trajectory lemma, the two approximation errors are zero.
step:trajectory-comparison.why_here: It supplies the general comparison estimate before the initial separation is specialized to zero.

fact:trajectory-comparison.title: Exponential separation bound
fact:trajectory-comparison.summary: For forward solutions under the one-sided comparison hypotheses, a separation at most δ at time a grows by at most the factor e raised to K(t−a) on the closed interval.
fact:trajectory-comparison.why_here: Forward uniqueness follows by setting the initial separation bound to zero.

step:one-sided-principle.title: Grönwall bound with zero initial distance
step:one-sided-principle.summary: Equal values at the left endpoint give the comparison lemma an initial distance bound of zero. Its exponential upper bound is then zero throughout the interval. Distance is nonnegative and vanishes only at equality, giving forward uniqueness.
step:one-sided-principle.why_here: This derives the reusable one-sided principle from the more general trajectory estimate.

fact:one-sided-principle.title: Forward uniqueness principle
fact:one-sided-principle.summary: Under the one-sided hypotheses, two solutions agreeing at the left endpoint agree on the entire forward interval.
fact:one-sided-principle.why_here: It applies directly to the later half and provides the principle used after reflecting the earlier half.

step:split-interval.title: Restrict to two half-intervals
step:split-interval.summary: The interior time t₀ splits [a,b] into [a,t₀] and [t₀,b]. The derivative and state-set hypotheses are needed on (a,t₀] on the left and [t₀,b) on the right, both subsets of (a,b). Ordinary derivatives restrict to the required one-sided derivatives, and continuity restricts to both closed halves.
step:split-interval.why_here: This gives each one-sided theorem the hypotheses it needs and supplies the cover used at the end.

fact:split-interval.title: Half-interval cover and restricted hypotheses
fact:split-interval.summary: The two closed halves cover the full interval, and each inherits the hypotheses for uniqueness in its direction of time.
fact:split-interval.why_here: The restricted hypotheses support both applications, and the cover combines their conclusions.

step:forward-agreement.title: Apply forward ODE uniqueness
step:forward-agreement.summary: On [t₀,b], the restricted hypotheses give right derivatives and the required state constraints. Equality at the left endpoint t₀ lets forward uniqueness give equality on the whole half-interval, including b.
step:forward-agreement.why_here: It applies the general forward theorem to the given pair of trajectories.

fact:forward-agreement.title: Agreement after the initial time
fact:forward-agreement.summary: The two given trajectories coincide from t₀ through b.
fact:forward-agreement.why_here: This supplies equality on the later part of the cover.

step:backward-agreement.title: Apply backward ODE uniqueness
step:backward-agreement.summary: On [a,t₀], the given curves agree at the right endpoint and satisfy the restricted left-derivative hypotheses. Backward uniqueness reflects time and uses the field −v(−t,y), since differentiating a reflected trajectory introduces a minus sign. Forward uniqueness of the reflected curves yields agreement from a through t₀.
step:backward-agreement.why_here: It applies the backward theorem to the given pair on the earlier half of the interval.

fact:backward-agreement.title: Agreement before the initial time
fact:backward-agreement.summary: The two given trajectories coincide from a through t₀.
fact:backward-agreement.why_here: This supplies equality on the earlier part of the cover.

step:agreement-on-interval.title: Combine equality on the two halves
step:agreement-on-interval.summary: Take any time in [a,b]. It belongs to at least one of the two closed halves, where the corresponding one-sided result gives equality. Thus the trajectories coincide on the full interval.
step:agreement-on-interval.why_here: It combines the two local applications into the conclusion of closed-interval uniqueness.

fact:agreement-on-interval.title: Agreement on the closed interval
fact:agreement-on-interval.summary: Under the hypotheses of the uniqueness argument, the two given trajectories agree at every time from a through b.
fact:agreement-on-interval.why_here: This is the explicit conclusion establishing the uniqueness theorem.

concepts.title: Spatial Lipschitz continuity
concepts.summary: At a fixed time, the distance between two field values is at most K times the distance between their states, provided both states lie in the permitted set.

concepts.title: Complete metric space of curves
concepts.summary: The supremum metric measures the largest pointwise separation. Uniform limits of continuous curves into a complete state space exist in that metric, and closed constraints such as a common Lipschitz bound pass to the limit.

concepts.title: Picard iteration
concepts.summary: Turn an ODE into an integral update by integrating the field along a candidate curve and adding the initial value. A curve fixed by the update satisfies the associated integral equation.

concepts.title: Factorial decay of iterate bounds
concepts.summary: Each integration of a power of elapsed time raises the exponent and divides by the new exponent. The resulting coefficient cⁿ/n! eventually falls below one for every fixed nonnegative c.

concepts.title: Banach’s fixed-point theorem
concepts.summary: A self-map with Lipschitz constant below one on a nonempty complete metric space has a unique fixed point. If a power of a map contracts, that power’s fixed point is also fixed by the map because the map commutes with its power.

concepts.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus
concepts.summary: Differentiating the integral of a continuous integrand with respect to the upper limit recovers the integrand. Within a closed interval, the derivative is tested using increments that remain in the interval.

concepts.title: Grönwall’s inequality
concepts.summary: A differential bound proportional to the size of a difference gives an exponential bound in terms of its initial size when the error term is zero. With zero initial size, the difference stays zero.

concepts.title: Time reversal
concepts.summary: Reflecting time converts a backward problem into a forward one. The chain rule changes the sign of the reflected vector field and exchanges left and right derivatives.

concepts.title: Equality on an interval cover
concepts.summary: If two functions agree on each subinterval of a cover, they agree at every point of the covered interval.
